title: Customer token amortization rollup service for mid-cycle plan changes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: When customers change plans or adjust reserved capacity mid-billing-cycle (upgrades, downgrades, or partial refunds), the current billing ingestion pipeline creates sharp discontinuities in per-token cost attribution. This causes noisy cost dashboards and inaccurate chargebacks for Dedicated customers. Goal: implement a deterministic, idempotent daily rollup job that amortizes token consumption and reserved capacity across a billing window so that per-customer token cost and reserved-vs-burst allocations are smooth, auditable, and reproducible. The job should produce a canonical amortized_token_cost record per customer per day that downstream billing and chargeback jobs consume. It must support backfills, handle retroactive plan changes, and integrate with existing usage-change events (plan_change, reservation_adjustment) and token_consumption stream.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic daily rollup job exists that emits amortized_token_cost(customer_id, date, tokens_amortized, reserved_tokens_allocated, burst_tokens, amortized_cost_usd) to the accounting topic/database

Rollups correctly reflect mid-cycle plan changes: upgrades prorate future days; downgrades create a negative amortization adjustment record for prior days where observed consumption exceeded entitlements
Job is idempotent and safe to re-run for arbitrary date ranges; backfill of historical months yields identical results to initial run
End-to-end tests and integration fixtures validate reconciliation against sample billing statements
Operational monitoring: job health metrics, SLA (start-to-finish < 90m for 30k customers), and alerting on >1% daily mismatch against source ledger samples
implementation_notes: Design: - Input streams: token_consumption_events (per request token counts), plan_change_events (effective timestamps and entitlements), reservation_commits (reserved capacity records), and existing token_ledger snapshots. - Core algorithm: windowed rollforward per customer using billing-day partitions. For each day, compute entitlement curve by applying plan_change_events in chronological order; amortize any reservation_commits across their commit window. Token consumption is attributed by day; when consumption > entitlement on a day, mark excess as burst_tokens and attribute cost at burst rate. When plan_change reduces entitlement retroactively (proration/refund), emit a negative amortization adjustment on the affected day(s). - Sharding: deterministic Murmur3(customer_id) % N to allow parallel idempotent processing. - State: use compacted Kafka topic (accounting-state) for last-run watermark and reconciliation checkpoints. Use Parquet daily snapshots in S3 for auditable export. - Performance: batch per-shard day windows, use vectorized aggregates, and push down time partition filters to avoid scanning entire history. - Failure handling: create tombstone record policy for deleted customers, retryable SQS/DLQ pattern for transient failures, and a light-weight dry-run mode for previewing outcomes. - Backfill strategy: incremental backfill using date ranges; ensure compaction and reprocessing produce the same amortized_token_cost output (idempotence via deterministic keys).
